summary: Canary rollforward blocked by stale routing-hint leading to silent fallback to compatibility variant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Cascadia Health, enterprise) reports intermittent quality regressions and increased inference latency after a scheduled canary rollforward for redwood-open/rlhf-v2-13b. Traffic for a subset of tenant sessions silently routed to redwood-compat/13b-compat (compat variant) during the rollforward window despite tenant pin expressed in API request metadata.

Impact:
- ~3% of requests from the customer during the 18:30-19:12 PST window returned compat-variant outputs (lower quality) and exhibited +120ms median latency.
- Customer-facing regression observed in live product tests; escalated by Customer Success.

Observed behavior differs from expected: pinned sessions should remain bound to explicitly-pinned model until manual or orchestrator-confirmed commit; fallback to compat-variant should only occur on active healthcheck eviction or explicit autoscale preemption.
impact: Customer-visible quality regressions and increased latency for enterprise production traffic; potential downstream alerting (SLO blip) and CS escalation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Schedule a canary rollforward that promotes redwood-open/rlhf-v2-13b to a higher weight in prod-us-west.
2) From a pinned-tenant session (header X-Tenant-Pin: <model:rlhf-v2-13b>), send a mix of chat requests and long-context streaming requests.
3) Observe routing decisions in edge logs and compare returned model tag in response metadata (X-Model-Served).
4) Inspect orchestrator snapshots and routing-hint cache for stale entries referencing pre-rollforward shard hints.
logs:
[2026-03-12T18:37:05Z] edge-proxy: tenant=casci-23 session=abcd1234 received request; pin=rlhf-v2-13b
[2026-03-12T18:37:05Z] routing-mesh: lookup -> hint-cache KEY:shard-hint:casci-23 => endpoint=orchestrator-node-7 (ttl=0m,stale)
[2026-03-12T18:37:05Z] orchestrator: route-decide -> selected=compat-13b (fallback_reason=stale_hint_resolve, health=ok)
[2026-03-12T18:37:06Z] serving-runtime: model-served=redwood-compat/13b-compat latency=220ms
[2026-03-12T18:37:06Z] edge-proxy: response headers X-Model-Served: redwood-compat/13b-compat
timeline: 18:20 PST - Scheduled canary rollforward initiated (weight bump + prewarm).
18:30 PST - Customer began seeing degraded outputs; CS opened an alert to Support.
18:40 PST - Support triage: observed discrepancy between tenant pin and served model headers.
18:55 PST - SRE pulled routing-hint cache and noticed multiple entries with ttl=0m marked stale but still returned by edge lookup.
19:05 PST - Temporary mitigation: forced routing-hint cache invalidation at edge and manual reassert of tenant pin; immediate reduction in regressions.
19:12 PST - Customer confirmed drop in observed regressions; incident escalation reduced to P1 support.
2026-03-13 - Ongoing: engineering investigating orchestrator hint-resolution code path and snapshot propagation race.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Edge hint-cache returns stale entries when orchestrator snapshot rotates quickly during rollforward, and the hint is interpreted as authoritative even for pinned sessions.
Hypothesis 2: Orchestrator's hint-to-route reconciliation contains a race where stale hint wins if health probe returns without explicit pin-override check.
Repro on staging: reproduced route selection to compat-variant when we accelerated snapshot rotation and disabled TTL enforcement for hint-cache (test flag).
Telemetry: token-level traces show X-Model-Requested=rlhf-v2-13b but X-Model-Served=13b-compat; route decision stamp lacks pin-check log line.
Edge debug: edge-proxy code path expects orchestrator route decision to include pin-override flag; missing in returned payload when snapshot is from 'legacy-shard' quickly retired.
mitigation: 1) Immediate: invalidated routing-hint cache across affected edge nodes for us-west; forced re-resolve to orchestrator snapshots and reasserted tenant pins. 2) Short-term: added monitoring alert on pin-request vs pin-served mismatch (>0.5% for enterprise customers).
planned_resolution: 1) Patch orchestrator to always evaluate explicit tenant pin precedence before honoring stale routing hints (PR in progress).
2) Add TTL enforcement and detect/blacklist stale hint entries returned with ttl<=0.
3) Add unit/integration tests to reproduce snapshot rotation race and ensure pin-check logging is present for every route decision.
comments: 2026-03-12T18:45Z - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reports 3/100 requests returned degraded outputs. Asked for sample request IDs and logs.
2026-03-12T18:52Z - SRE-Team (SRE): Pulling edge hint-cache; seeing entries with ttl=0m marked 'stale' but still returned by lookup. Investigating orchestrator snapshot timing.
2026-03-12T19:08Z - Liam O'Connor (Oncall Eng): Performed forced cache invalidation; customer reports improvement. Creating follow-up engineering ticket for orchestrator fix. Linked SUP-3141592.
2026-03-13T09:15Z - Product (J. Martinez): Requesting risk assessment for including TTL enforcement in next canary hardening release; wants ETA for fix.
resolution_summary: TBD - temporary mitigation (routing-hint cache invalidation and pin reassert) resolved customer impact for now. Root cause appears to be stale hint handling during rapid orchestrator snapshot rotations; permanent fix planned.
notes_for_postmortem: Verify that explicit tenant pins are treated as highest precedence across all routing layers (edge, orchestrator, serving).
Add canary hardening checklist entry: ensure routing-hint TTLs are not allowed to reach zero while snapshot rotation in flight.
Review and harden edge/orchestrator contract for route-decision payload to include pin-evaluation flag.
